html:
Parameswara was the last king of Singapura and the founder of Malacca on the Malay peninsula, around 1400. Malacca soon became the main port of the Strait of Malacca and the seat of the Malacca Sultanate.

He was a prince of Palembang in Sumatra who claimed descent from the kings of Srivijaya. After a quarrel with Majapahit he fled to Singapura, took power there, and was driven out in turn, by a Majapahit attack in the account of the Malay Annals. He settled at the mouth of the Malacca River, a good harbour where the monsoon winds meet.

To protect his new town from Siam and Java he turned to Ming China. The admiral Zheng He stopped at Malacca on his voyages, and in 1411 Parameswara himself sailed to China to visit the Yongle Emperor. Under Chinese protection Malacca drew traders from India, Arabia, China and the islands. He may have become a Muslim late in life, and his successors made Malacca a centre for spreading Islam through the region.
sum: Parameswara was the last king of Singapura and the founder of Malacca on the Malay peninsula, around 1400. Malacca soon became the main port of the Strait of Malacca and the seat of the Malacca Sultanate.
